Raw daily data, CSV files and validation codes

Source: vignettes/daily-data-and-quality.Rmd
daily-data-and-quality.Rmd
library(meteogal2fdata)

Daily observations and validation codes

The MeteoGalicia daily JSON service returns, for each measurement, the value (valor), its unit (unidade) and a validation code (lnCodigoValidacion). The code belongs to an individual measurement, not to the complete station-day: temperature and precipitation recorded on the same day can therefore have different validation codes.

meteogal_qc_codes()
#>   code        description default usable
#> 1    0      Not validated   FALSE   TRUE
#> 2    1     Valid original    TRUE   TRUE
#> 3    2            Suspect   FALSE   TRUE
#> 4    3          Erroneous   FALSE  FALSE
#> 5    5 Valid interpolated    TRUE   TRUE
#> 6    9       Not recorded   FALSE  FALSE

The package uses English variable names and keeps each code in a separate qc_<variable> column. For example, daily mean temperature is stored as temp_mean and its validation code as qc_temp_mean.

The original MeteoGalicia parameter identifiers can still be supplied to vars when necessary, but the standard output names are intentionally kept simple and consistent across the package.

Download raw data: nothing is filtered

meteogal2download() stores the values and validation codes as delivered by MeteoGalicia. The download stage does not decide which observations should be used statistically. Files are written by station and year, either as RDS or as UTF-8 CSV.

The following example uses two deliberately contrasting stations: Coruña-Torre de Hércules (10157), on the Atlantic coast, and Ourense (10148), inland.

log <- meteogal2download(
  start_date = "2023-01-01",
  end_date = "2024-12-31",
  station_ids = c("10157", "10148"),
  vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"),
  format = "csv",
  out_dir = "meteogal_daily"
)
log

raw <- read.csv(
  file.path("meteogal_daily", "10157", "10157_2024.csv"),
  colClasses = c(station_id = "character"),
  encoding = "UTF-8"
)
head(raw[, c("fecha", "temp_mean", "qc_temp_mean", "prec", "qc_prec")])

Provenance

The file out_dir/_meteogal_manifest.csv records how station-year files were obtained. A new row is added whenever a file is written.

read.csv(file.path("meteogal_daily", "_meteogal_manifest.csv"))
column content
file, station_id, year, format file written
n_rows, first_date, last_date temporal coverage
id_param, variables requested and stored parameters
qc_codes whether validation-code columns are present
quality_filter always records that downloaded values are unfiltered
downloaded_utc, source, package_version provenance

RDS files also keep provenance in attr(x, "meteogal_meta") and units in attr(x, "units").

Choose the quality criterion when reading

Downloaded files can be read repeatedly using different validation criteria, without downloading the observations again.

valid <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily")
original <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily", quality = 1)
recent <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily", quality = c(0, 1, 5))
all_usable <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily", quality = NULL)

The default is quality = c(1, 5): valid original observations and values interpolated by MeteoGalicia. Values with other codes become NA in the returned measurement column, while their validation codes remain available. Codes 3 (erroneous) and 9 (not recorded), and the sentinel value -9999, are always treated as missing.

A small artificial example illustrates only the filtering mechanics; it is not MeteoGalicia data:

toy <- data.frame(
  fecha = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:5,
  station_id = "toy",
  temp_mean = c(10.1, 10.4, 35.0, 9.8, 9.9, -9999),
  qc_temp_mean = c(1L, 5L, 2L, 0L, 3L, 9L)
)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(toy, f, row.names = FALSE)
meteogal2df(data_dir = f)
#> [MeteoGalicia] quality = c(1, 5): values set to NA: 1 with code 0 (Not validated); 1 with code 2 (Suspect); 1 with code 3 (Erroneous); 1 with code 9 (Not recorded). Codes are kept in the qc_ columns; see meteogal_qc_codes().
#>        fecha station_id temp_mean qc_temp_mean
#> 1 2024-01-01        toy      10.1            1
#> 2 2024-01-02        toy      10.4            5
#> 3 2024-01-03        toy        NA            2
#> 4 2024-01-04        toy        NA            0
#> 5 2024-01-05        toy        NA            3
#> 6 2024-01-06        toy        NA            9
meteogal2df(data_dir = f, quality = c(0, 1, 2, 5))
#> [MeteoGalicia] quality = c(0, 1, 2, 5): values set to NA: 1 with code 3 (Erroneous); 1 with code 9 (Not recorded). Codes are kept in the qc_ columns; see meteogal_qc_codes().
#>        fecha station_id temp_mean qc_temp_mean
#> 1 2024-01-01        toy      10.1            1
#> 2 2024-01-02        toy      10.4            5
#> 3 2024-01-03        toy      35.0            2
#> 4 2024-01-04        toy       9.8            0
#> 5 2024-01-05        toy        NA            3
#> 6 2024-01-06        toy        NA            9

Missing data

The package does not impute, interpolate or smooth observations:

  • station-days absent from the service response are absent from the daily data frame;
  • missing observations, -9999, codes 3 and 9, and values rejected by quality are represented as NA;
  • functional objects use a 365-day grid, and missing days remain NA;
  • values with code 5 are values already interpolated by MeteoGalicia, not by meteogal2fdata.

Bundled real example

data-raw/build-example.R creates a two-station example for 2023-2024 using Coruña-Torre de Hércules and Ourense. The example contains the raw values and validation codes returned by the service.

f <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_example.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
if (nzchar(f)) {
  ex <- meteogal2df(data_dir = f, quality = NULL)
  print(unique(ex[, c("station_id", "station_name")]))
  print(table(ex$station_id, ex$qc_temp_mean, useNA = "ifany"))
} else {
  f <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_small.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
  ex <- meteogal2df(data_dir = f)
  ex[, c("fecha", "station_id", "temp_mean", "prec")]
}
#>     station_id             station_name
#> 1        10148                  Ourense
#> 732      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules
#>        
#>           1
#>   10148 731
#>   10157 731
